service.name: Wedding music in Colorado Springs
service.serviceType: Live music for weddings in Colorado Springs: ceremony guitarist, cocktail hour duo, band and DJ
service.description: Live wedding music in Colorado Springs and the Pikes Peak region: an acoustic or Spanish guitarist for the ceremony, an acoustic or jazz duo for cocktail hour, a band or open-format DJ for the reception, on one contract with sound included and one flat Front Range travel line.

faqs.q: Do you play weddings in Colorado Springs?
faqs.a: Yes, the whole day or any one part of it. Colorado Springs is a Front Range drive from Denver, so the music is quoted at the same fee a Denver wedding sees, with one flat travel line for the run down I-25 and back and no lodging line. The Broadmoor, Garden of the Gods Resort and Club, Cheyenne Mountain Resort, The Mining Exchange and The Antlers are the venues that come up most.

faqs.q: Can a guitarist play an outdoor ceremony in Colorado Springs?
faqs.a: Yes, and outdoors is where most Springs ceremonies happen. A guitarist needs a covered, level and dry spot with power run to it, sets up in 6 by 4 feet, and plays the prelude, processional and recessional through a small system that also carries an announcement microphone for the officiant. The afternoon wind off the range is the thing to plan for, so the ceremony spot and the move-indoors call are agreed before the day.

faqs.q: Is a duo enough for a Colorado Springs cocktail hour?
faqs.a: For the guest counts a resort terrace holds at cocktail hour, yes. Two musicians hold 65 to 72 dBA at the nearest table, which is a level guests who have just met can talk across, and they fit an 8 by 6 foot corner on one circuit. The trio is the size to book when the crowd spreads across a full ballroom or the hour has dancing in it.

faqs.q: Band or DJ for a Colorado Springs reception?
faqs.a: Often both, in sequence. A live act through dinner and the first hour of the floor, then the DJ carrying the late end through the same sound system on the same contract, is the configuration most receptions settle on. A band alone suits a wedding that wants the whole evening watched; a DJ alone suits a late floor and a tighter budget.

faqs.q: What does the Colorado Springs travel line cover?
faqs.a: The drive down from Denver and back for the musicians and the gear, as one flat figure on the quote. There's no mileage arithmetic and no lodging line, because Colorado Springs is a Front Range date rather than a mountain one. Load-in runs 45 to 60 minutes at these sizes through whichever door the venue prefers.

faqs.q: How far ahead should we book wedding musicians in Colorado Springs?
faqs.a: Couples in wedding forums report booking music nine to fourteen months out, after the venue and before most of the rest of the list. Tell us the date and we'll come back quickly with an answer and a price for that day.
